verdict.root_cause: Every failing checkout trace aborts at one leaf call: the CartService GetCart RPC issued by checkoutservice inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart. That span carries ERROR in all ~39 failing traces and returns in 2.0-4.7ms, and checkoutservice/frontend spans inherit the ERROR unchanged [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc]. checkoutservice logs corroborate: placement lines continue steadily through 05:56:57 but payment, email and message-write completion lines vanish after ~05:53, with no error severity anywhere [tr_487c74c4c885]. So cartservice is returning fast deterministic errors to checkoutservice, and the downstream alerts on shipping/currency/email/accounting follow from a checkout flow that never reaches them. Why cartservice is erroring is not established — no dispatch queried cartservice's logs, metrics, change history or its cache backend — so the mechanism inside cartservice is undetermined.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the ERROR origin to the cart boundary and rule out payment, email, currency and shipping because no such span is ever reached [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc]. checkoutservice is exonerated as origin: empty change log [tr_d77171caf2d9], process alive and serving [tr_487c74c4c885], and its PlaceOrder duration is consumed by the child GetCart with the intermediate span unmarked [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc]. paymentservice is exonerated by clean paired charge/complete logs [tr_5b0b3632e058] and no changes [tr_01b6dcb5205a]. The flat 0.66 error ratio (sd 0.016) matches a deterministic per-request failure on one path, not saturation [tr_8ffe1069f495]. Sub-5ms GetCart spans with no timeout-length span argue against dependency_latency [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc]. Distinguishing bad_config, bad_deploy or resource_exhaustion inside cartservice needs cartservice evidence that was never gathered, so fault_class stays unknown rather than guessed.
open_questions: cartservice was never queried directly: no logs, error metrics, change history or restart/OOM record for it.
Is cartservice's Redis/cache backend healthy? A failed cache dependency would produce exactly these fast GetCart errors.
True onset time is unpinned: the checkoutservice baseline window returned no samples [tr_8ffe1069f495] and 05:25-05:53 of its logs is truncated [tr_487c74c4c885].

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice's cache/Redis backend is unavailable or refusing connections, and cartservice converts that into an immediate GetCart error.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible as the layer below, but the failure is a fast rejection not a wait — no timeout-length spans exist [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc] — and no cache telemetry was collected to confirm it.

alternatives.root_cause: An unrecorded cartservice deploy or config push shortly before 05:55 introduced a broken cart read path.
alternatives.why_not: No change query was ever run against cartservice; the empty change logs cover only checkoutservice and paymentservice [tr_d77171caf2d9, tr_01b6dcb5205a], so this is speculation with no supporting record.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no change in any signal is expected. The fault localization is solid — every failing trace aborts at the checkoutservice->CartService GetCart leaf span, returning ERROR in 2.0-4.7ms [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc], and checkoutservice sustains a ~0.66 error ratio with no error-severity logs of its own [tr_8ffe1069f495, tr_487c74c4c885] — but no permitted action's preconditions are met against cartservice. rollback_image and revert_config both require a recorded prior image/config and an in-window change named by the evidence; cartservice's change history was never queried, so neither precondition can be shown to hold. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and the evidence points the other way: the errors are fast, deterministic and uniform across all ~39 traces [tr_92d8f3f4c6cc], which is the signature of a rejected call or a failing backend dependency, not a degraded or wedged process. scale_service is unavailable in this world. The correct next step is investigative, not remedial: query cartservice's logs, error metrics, change history, and the health of its Redis/cache backend, and recover the truncated 05:25-05:53 checkoutservice log range to pin true onset.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a cartservice query returns a deploy, image change, or config push inside the incident window — then rollback_image or revert_config becomes proposable with a real precondition. It is also wrong if cartservice logs show OOM kills, restart counts climbing, or a crash-loop banner, which would make restart_service the indicated class. Conversely, if cartservice logs show clean startup, a single stable process, and connection-refused or auth errors against its cache backend, then no action on this allowlist addresses the mechanism at all and the abstention stands permanently rather than provisionally.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued user-visible checkout failure: roughly two thirds of checkout calls keep erroring and the shipping, currency, email and accounting alerts keep firing while investigation proceeds. That is a real cost. It is preferable to the alternative: a restart of cartservice would discard its in-process cache and, if the mechanism is a failing external cache backend or a bad config, would either do nothing or lengthen the outage by adding a cold-cache period on top of an unfixed fault — and restart_service is explicitly irreversible.
proposal.blast_radius: No one — nothing changes. The services currently affected remain affected: checkoutservice and frontend carry the inherited ERROR on every cart-dependent trace, loadgenerator continues to observe failures, and shippingservice, currencyservice, emailservice, accountingservice and frauddetectionservice continue to see the drop in downstream traffic from a checkout flow that never reaches them.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting starting at checkout/frontend and fanning out to nearly every downstream within 90 seconds; no open incident covers it. Fault class is unclear from alerts alone — checkout-centric shared dependency or deploy are both plausible.
